mainTopic: Laws of a damaged, altered, or patched שופר, hearing through echoes, כוונה, and blowing into a pit
overview: This עמוד finishes the משנה about damaged שופרות. A patched hole matters only if it blocks the blowing. Blowing into a pit counts only if the real שופר sound was heard, and a passerby who hears the שופר or the מגילה fulfills his obligation only with כוונה. The גמרא brings ברייתות about a שופר that was shortened, scraped, plated with gold, placed inside another שופר, or turned around. רב פפא explains that 'turned around' means its ends were reversed, which is unfit because a שופר must be blown the way it grew (רב מתנה on 'וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ'). Next come additions and patches, where רבי נתן allows a horn patch, and רבי יוחנן's limit on this is taught in two versions. The ברייתא then rules on cracks, defines the minimum size of a שופר, and says every natural sound is fit. רב אשי explains a ruling about a drilled horn, and רב הונא explains that blowing into a pit counts for those standing inside it but not for those at its edge. The עמוד ends as רבה begins a statement that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A punctured שופר that was sealed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a patched hole makes the שופר unfit only if the patch still blocks the blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a שופר got a hole and someone sealed it: if the hole still gets in the way of the blowing, it is unfit. If not, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of damaged שופרות and gives the rule for one that had a hole and was patched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The patch alone does not make the שופר unfit. The question is only whether the blowing is still blocked, so a good repair leaves the שופר fit.

keyTerms.meaning: It was punctured or got a hole
Blocks or gets in the way
Unfit, not usable for the מצוה

phrases.english: If it was punctured and he sealed it,
if it impedes the blowing — it is unfit,
but if not — it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of damaged שופרות, which began on the previous עמוד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sealed hole makes the שופר unfit only if it still impedes the blowing

steps.title: Blowing into a pit or a large jug
steps.stepSummary: If someone blows a שופר into a hollow space, it counts only if the listener heard the real שופר sound and not an echo.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone blows into a pit, a cistern, or a big jug: if the listener heard the sound of the שופר, he fulfilled his obligation. If he heard only an echo, he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from damage to the שופר itself to a problem with where the sound is heard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obligation is to hear the sound of a שופר. Inside a hollow space the sound can bounce back as an echo, and an echo is not a שופר sound. So it all depends on what actually reached the listener's ears.

phrases.english: One who blows into a pit
or into a cistern
or into a large jug,
if he heard the sound of the shofar — he has fulfilled his obligation,
phrases.notes: "He" here means the person listening, who may be standing outside the pit.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם קוֹל הֲבָרָה שָׁמַע — לָא יָצָא.
phrases.english: but if he heard the sound of an echo — he has not fulfilled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the condition of the שופר to the way its sound is heard
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One fulfills the obligation only by hearing the real שופר sound, not an echo

steps.title: Hearing from outside the בית הכנסת needs כוונה
steps.stepSummary: Someone who hears the שופר or the מגילה from outside fulfills his obligation only if he intended to. Two people can hear the same sound, and only the one with intent fulfills it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, someone walking behind the בית הכנסת, or whose house is next to it, who hears the שופר or the reading of the מגילה: if he had in mind to fulfill his obligation, he did. If not, he did not. Two people can both hear it, but only the one who intended fulfills it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new requirement. Besides hearing the right sound, the listener must have כוונה, meaning he means to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a passerby, someone who could easily hear the sound without thinking about it. The משנה says hearing alone is not enough. The last line stresses that the very same sound can count for one person and not for another, depending only on his intent.

keyTerms.meaning: He directed his heart, meaning he intended to fulfill the מצוה
The scroll of אסתר read on פורים

steps.whatToRemember: Two things are needed: hearing the real שופר sound, and having כוונה to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is a central source for the idea that a מצוה like hearing the שופר or the מגילה requires intent.

phrases.english: And similarly, one who was passing
behind a synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בֵּיתוֹ סָמוּךְ לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת,
phrases.english: or whose house was next to the synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁמַע קוֹל שׁוֹפָר אוֹ קוֹל מְגִילָּה,
phrases.english: and he heard the sound of the shofar or the sound of the Megillah,
if he directed his heart — he has fulfilled his obligation,
but if not — he has not fulfilled it.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּה שָׁמַע וְזֶה שָׁמַע,
phrases.english: Even though this one heard and that one heard,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה כִּוֵּון לִבּוֹ, וְזֶה לֹא כִּוֵּון לִבּוֹ.
phrases.english: this one directed his heart, and that one did not direct his heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁהָיָה עוֹבֵר אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The word וכן links it to the previous case: just as the right sound is needed, so is the right intent
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hearing the שופר or מגילה counts only with כוונה to fulfill the obligation

steps.title: A ברייתא: a shortened or scraped שופר is fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא: a שופר that was cut shorter, or scraped down until it was thin, is still fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if a שופר was long and someone shortened it, it is fit. If he scraped it down to a thin layer, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that lists more changes to a שופר and says which ones are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting the שופר shorter or making it thinner does not turn it into something else. It is still a שופר, so it stays fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Its thin outer skin or layer

phrases.english: Gemara
The Rabbis taught:
If it was long and he shortened it — it is fit.
If he scraped it and brought it down to its thin layer — it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא that adds cases to the משנה's laws of altered שופרות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shortening or thinning a שופר does not make it unfit

steps.title: A שופר plated with gold
steps.stepSummary: Gold plating where the mouth goes, or on the inside, makes the שופר unfit. Gold elsewhere is fine. Gold on the outside is fine unless it changes the sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he covered it with gold where the mouth is placed, it is unfit. Somewhere else, it is fit. If he covered the inside with gold, it is unfit. If he covered the outside: if the sound changed from what it was before, it is unfit. If not, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with cases of a שופר covered in gold, and the answer depends on where the gold is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mouth touches gold, or the air passes through gold, the person is blowing gold and not horn. Gold on the outside is only decoration, unless it changes the sound so that it is no longer the sound of the שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the mouth is put

phrases.aramaic: צִיפָּהוּ זָהָב בִּמְקוֹם הַנָּחַת פֶּה — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: If he plated it with gold at the place where the mouth is put — it is unfit.
Not at the place where the mouth is put — it is fit.
If he plated it with gold on the inside — it is unfit.

phrases.aramaic: מִבַּחוּץ, אִם נִשְׁתַּנָּה קוֹלוֹ מִכְּמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה — פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: On the outside: if its sound changed from what it was — it is unfit,
but if not — it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with cases of gold plating
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gold at the mouthpiece or inside makes it unfit; gold outside makes it unfit only if it changes the sound

steps.title: The ברייתא repeats the rule of a sealed hole
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא includes the same rule found in the משנה: a patched hole matters only if it blocks the blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was punctured and he sealed it: if it impedes the blowing, it is unfit. If not, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats word for word the rule about a patched hole that the משנה gave in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the law here. The ברייתא simply includes this case in its own full list of altered שופרות.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new case. It is the same wording as the משנה in step 1, now appearing again as part of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: If it was punctured and he sealed it,
if it impedes the blowing — it is unfit,
but if not — it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and repeats the משנה's rule from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sealed hole makes the שופר unfit only if it impedes the blowing

steps.title: One שופר placed inside another
steps.stepSummary: If one שופר is placed inside another and blown, it counts only if the listener heard the inner שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put one שופר inside another: if he heard the sound of the inner one, he fulfilled his obligation. If he heard the sound of the outer one, he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the case of two שופרות, one inside the other, and asks which sound reached the listener.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the inner שופר's sound is heard, the listener heard one plain שופר. If the outer one is heard, the sound passed through both of them, so it was not the sound of one שופר.
steps.whatToRemember: Throughout the ברייתא, the test is whether what is heard is still the true sound of one שופר.

phrases.english: If he placed a shofar inside a shofar,
if he heard the sound of the inner one — he has fulfilled his obligation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם קוֹל חִיצוֹן שָׁמַע — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: but if he heard the sound of the outer one — he has not fulfilled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case of the ברייתא, again tested by whether the sound is that of a single שופר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the sound of the inner שופר counts; the outer שופר's sound does not

steps.title: A second ברייתא: scraping a שופר, and a שופר inside a שופר
steps.stepSummary: A שופר that was scraped, inside or outside, even down to a thin outer layer, is still כשר. If one שופר is placed inside another, it counts only if you heard the inner one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: if someone scraped a שופר, inside or outside, it is fit. Even if he scraped it until only its thin outer layer was left, it is still fit. If he put one שופר inside another and blew: if he heard the inner שופר's sound, he fulfilled his obligation. If he heard the outer one's sound, he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא that says scraping a שופר does not make it unfit, even if very little is left. It also repeats the rule about a שופר inside a שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scraping only removes material from the same horn, so it is still the original שופר. Step 4 already allowed scraping down to the thin layer; what is new here is that scraping on the inside or the outside is equally fine. The 'שופר inside a שופר' rule matches step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Its thin outer layer, like a skin
The sound of the inner שופר
The sound of the outer שופר

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: גֵּרְדוֹ, בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ — כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: If he scraped it, whether on the inside or on the outside, it is fit.
If he scraped it until it was left with only its thin layer, it is fit.
If he placed a shofar inside a shofar,
if he heard the sound of the inner one, he has fulfilled his obligation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם קוֹל חִיצוֹן שָׁמַע — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: but if he heard the sound of the outer one, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גֵּרְדוֹ, בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ — כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא that adds to the rulings of the first ברייתא (steps 4–7).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scraping a שופר, even down to its thin outer layer, does not make it unfit. With a שופר inside a שופר, only the sound of the inner one counts.

steps.title: A שופר that was turned around
steps.stepSummary: If someone 'turned the שופר around' and blew it, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he turned it around and blew it, he did not fulfill his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives one more case: a שופר that was turned around does not work. The meaning of 'turned around' is not clear yet, and the next step explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first change in this ברייתא that makes the שופר unfit. It sets up רב פפא's explanation of what 'turned around' means.

phrases.english: If he turned it around and blew it, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last ruling of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A turned-around שופר is unfit for the מצוה.

steps.title: רב פפא explains what 'turned around' means
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says it does not mean turned inside out like a shirt. It means the narrow end was widened and the wide end was narrowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Don't think it means he turned it inside out like a shirt. Rather, it means he widened the narrow end and narrowed the wide end.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains a word in the ברייתא. 'Turned around' means the שופר's shape was reversed end to end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might picture softening the horn and flipping it inside out like clothing. רב פפא rejects that picture. The case is reshaping the horn so the mouthpiece end becomes wide and the wide end becomes narrow, so it is blown the opposite way from how it grew.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a shirt or tunic (turned inside out)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't picture the שופר being flipped inside out. רב פפא says it is reversed end to end, so the narrow side became wide and the wide side became narrow.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Do not say that he turned it inside out like a tunic,
rather, that he widened the narrow end
and narrowed the wide end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case of 'turned around' from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Turned around' means the שופר's ends were reversed in width, not turned inside out.

steps.title: Why does reversing the ends make the שופר unfit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason a reversed שופר does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the reversed שופר is unfit. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing was added and nothing is missing. It is the same horn, only reshaped, so a reason is needed.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רב פפא's case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a שופר with its ends reversed is unfit.

steps.title: The reason, from רב מתנה: blow it the way it grew
steps.stepSummary: The reason follows רב מתנה, who reads the word 'וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ' as saying the שופר must be used in the direction it was carried on the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רב מתנה, because רב מתנה said: the פסוק says 'וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ'. We need the שופר to be the way it was carried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רב מתנה's reading of the פסוק. The שופר has to keep the direction it had on the animal's head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ' sounds like 'carrying' or 'passing along.' רב מתנה learns from it that the שופר must be blown the way it grew on the animal. Reversing the ends breaks that direction, so the שופר is unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall sound,' from the root of carrying or passing along
The way it was carried (on the animal)

steps.whatToRemember: A שופר must be blown the way it grew on the animal. Scraping it is fine, but reversing its ends makes it unfit.

phrases.english: It is like Rav Mattana's view.
For Rav Mattana said:
"And you shall sound" —
we need it the way it was carried.
phrases.notes: He means the way the horn sat on the animal's head: narrow tip at one end, wide base at the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ' requires the שופר to be used in the direction it grew, so reversing its ends makes it unfit.

steps.title: Glued pieces, additions, and patched holes are unfit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says glued-together pieces of שופרות are unfit. A ברייתא adds that adding anything to a שופר, or patching a hole in it, makes it unfit whatever the patch is made of.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he glued together broken pieces of שופרות, it is unfit. The Sages taught: if he added anything at all to it, of the same material or a different material, it is unfit. If it got a hole and he sealed it, with the same material or a different material, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about glued pieces. Then it brings a ברייתא that applies the same idea to additions and patched holes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scraping takes material away, but these cases add something onto the horn, and that is not allowed. The first opinion in the ברייתא says it does not matter whether the addition is horn or something else. Either way the שופר is unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: With its own kind (the same material, horn)
Not with its own kind (a different material)
It got a hole and he sealed it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 6. There the hole only mattered if it blocked the blowing. Here the first opinion says any patch makes it unfit, and רבי נתן will disagree next.

phrases.english: If he glued together broken pieces of shofarot, it is unfit.
The Sages taught:
If he added to it any amount at all,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּמִינוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינוֹ — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: whether of its own kind or not of its own kind, it is unfit.
If it was punctured and he sealed it,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּמִינוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִינוֹ — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: whether with its own kind or not with its own kind, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּיבֵּק שִׁבְרֵי שׁוֹפָרוֹת — פָּסוּל. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה, about glued pieces.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Glued pieces, any addition, or any patched hole makes a שופר unfit, whether the added material is horn or something else.

steps.title: רבי נתן: a patch of horn is fine
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן disagrees. A hole sealed with the same material is כשר, and only a different material makes it פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: with its own kind, it is fit. Not with its own kind, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן disagrees with the first opinion about a patched hole. He allows a patch made of horn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נתן, a horn patch blends in with the שופר and counts as part of it. A patch of a different material is something foreign, so the שופר is unfit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
with its own kind, it is fit;
not with its own kind, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole sealed with horn is fit. A hole sealed with another material is unfit.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits רבי נתן: most of the שופר must remain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a horn patch is fine only when most of the original שופר is still there.
steps.simpleTranslation: About 'with its own kind it is fit,' רבי יוחנן said: that is only when most of it remained.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a condition to רבי נתן's ruling. A horn patch is acceptable only if most of the original שופר is intact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the patch is small and most of the original horn is there, it is still the same שופר. If the patch is a large part of it, the שופר is mostly new material and becomes unfit even according to רבי נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when (a condition)

phrases.english: "With its own kind, it is fit":
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting רבי נתן's words from step 14 before commenting on them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
This is only where most of it remained.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמִינוֹ כָּשֵׁר — אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְהוּא שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּיֵּיר רוּבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on רבי נתן's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole sealed with horn is fit only if most of the original שופר remains.

steps.title: So a patch of a different material is always unfit
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוחנן's words, the גמרא concludes that a patch of a different material makes the שופר unfit even when most of it remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: From this we learn that with a different material, even if most of it remained, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רבי יוחנן. Since he gave the 'most remains' condition only for a horn patch, a patch of a different material is unfit no matter what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition 'most of it remains' only helps a patch of the same material. A foreign material does not count as part of the שופר at all, so even a small patch of it makes the שופר unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: From this we can infer that

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי נתן as רבי יוחנן explains him: a horn patch is fine only if most of the שופר remains. A patch of any other material is always unfit.

phrases.english: By inference, with something not of its own kind,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּיֵּיר רוּבּוֹ — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: even though most of it remained, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from רבי יוחנן's condition.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A שופר patched with a different material is unfit even when most of the original remains. Only a horn patch can be fit, and only if most of the שופר remains.

steps.title: A second version: רבי יוחנן's limit applies to a different-material patch
steps.stepSummary: Some teach רבי יוחנן's words as going on the last part of the ברייתא. A patch of a different material makes the שופר unfit only when most of the original שופר was missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people attach this teaching to the last part of the ברייתא, which says that a patch not made of the same material makes the שופר unfit. On that, רבי יוחנן said this is only when most of the שופר was missing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way some people taught רבי יוחנן's statement. In this version, his words explain the 'different material makes it unfit' rule instead of the 'same material is fine' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Steps 15-16), רבי יוחנן limited the leniency: a same-material patch is only fine when most of the שופר remains. Here he limits the strictness instead. A different-material patch only makes the שופר unfit when most of it was missing. That means a small foreign patch would be acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (a second version of the same teaching)
The last clause of a teaching
Not of its own kind (a patch made of a different material)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first version the limit made the lenient rule stricter. In this version the limit makes the strict rule more lenient.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on the last clause:
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבי יוחנן's statement from Step 15. The 'last clause' is רבי נתן's rule about a different material.

phrases.english: [If sealed] not with its own kind, it is unfit;
Rabbi Yochanan said:
And that is only where most of it was missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבי יוחנן's statement from Step 15, attached to the other half of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A patch of a different material makes the שופר unfit only when most of the original שופר was missing.

steps.title: Inference: a same-material patch is always fine
steps.stepSummary: From this second version, the גמרא concludes that a patch of the same material is fine even when most of the שופר was missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This tells us that if the patch is the same material, the שופר is fit even if most of it was missing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the second version of רבי יוחנן's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן limited his ruling only to the different-material case. So the same-material case has no limit at all. In the first version (Step 15), a same-material patch was fine only if most of the שופר remained.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; from what was said, we learn
With its own kind (a patch of the same material)

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1: a same-material patch is fine only if most of the שופר remains, and any foreign patch makes it unfit. Version 2: a same-material patch is always fine, and a foreign patch makes it unfit only if most of the שופר was missing.

phrases.english: By implication, [if sealed] with its own kind,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּפְחַת רוּבּוֹ — כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: even if most of it was missing, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the logical result of the second version, the same way Step 16 did for the first version.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the second version, a same-material patch never makes the שופר unfit, no matter how much was missing.

steps.title: A שופר coated with gold
steps.stepSummary: Gold coating on the inside makes the שופר unfit. Gold coating on the outside makes it unfit only if it changes the sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone coated the שופר with gold on the inside, it is unfit. If the coating is on the outside, it is unfit if the sound changed from what it was before, and fit if the sound did not change.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a new case: a שופר coated with gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the inside and the outside differently. Gold on the inside is always a problem. Gold on the outside only matters if it changes the sound of the שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: On the inside / on the outside

phrases.english: If he coated it with gold on the inside, it is unfit.
On the outside:

phrases.aramaic: אִם נִשְׁתַּנָּה קוֹלוֹ מִכְּמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה — פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: if its sound changed from what it was, it is unfit;
and if not, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to quoting the ברייתא from Step 13, now with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gold coating on the inside makes a שופר unfit. Gold coating on the outside makes it unfit only if it changes the sound.

steps.title: A cracked שופר: along its length or across its width
steps.stepSummary: A crack along the length makes the שופר unfit. A crack across the width is fine only if enough of the שופר is left to blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the שופר cracked along its length, it is unfit. If it cracked across its width, it is fit if a piece big enough for blowing is still left, and unfit if not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the rules for a cracked שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A crack running along the length makes the whole שופר unfit. A crack going across only cuts off the part past the crack. So what matters is whether the part that is left is still big enough. The ברייתא calls this size the 'שיעור תקיעה' but does not yet say how big that is, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Along its length / across its width
The minimum size needed for blowing

phrases.english: If it cracked along its length, it is unfit.
Across its width:

phrases.aramaic: אִם נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר בּוֹ שִׁיעוּר תְּקִיעָה — כָּשֵׁר,
phrases.english: if there remains in it the measure for blowing, it is fit;
phrases.notes: This means the part of the שופר above the crack, the end you blow from.

phrases.english: and if not, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with another kind of damage to a שופר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A crack along the length makes a שופר unfit. A crack across the width is fine if enough remains for blowing.

steps.title: How big is 'enough for blowing'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how much is the minimum size needed for blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is the minimum size for blowing?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question to define the size it just mentioned. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about a crack across the width depends on knowing the minimum size of a שופר. So the ברייתא stops to explain what that size is.

phrases.english: And how much is the measure for blowing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact meaning of a term used in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum length a שופר must have to be acceptable.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן גמליאל: it must stick out past the hand on both sides
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן גמליאל explains that the שופר must be long enough to be held in the hand and still be seen sticking out on both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן גמליאל explained: long enough that when he holds it in his hand, it can be seen sticking out on this side and on that side.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן גמליאל answers the question and gives the minimum size of a שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The size is measured with a hand that is gripping the שופר. If the שופר shows on both sides of the closed hand, it is long enough.

keyTerms.meaning: On this side and on that side

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel explained:
enough that he can hold it in his hand
and it is seen [sticking out] on this side and on that side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The minimum size is enough that the שופר sticks out on both sides of the hand holding it.

steps.title: Every kind of שופר sound is acceptable
steps.stepSummary: A שופר whose sound is thin, thick, or rough is still fit, because every sound from a שופר is acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If its sound was thin, thick, or rough, it is fit, because all sounds are fit in a שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a rule that a שופר does not need any particular kind of sound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule fits with the gold case in Step 19. There the problem was a sound changed by something added to the שופר, not the natural sound of the שופר itself. As long as the sound comes from the שופר, any tone is fine.
steps.whatToRemember: How a שופר naturally sounds does not matter. What matters is whether it is whole and long enough, and whether its sound was changed by something added to it.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה קוֹלוֹ דַּק אוֹ עָבֶה אוֹ צָרוּר — כָּשֵׁר,
phrases.english: If its sound was thin, or thick, or rough, it is fit,
for all sounds are fit [in a שופר].
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה קוֹלוֹ דַּק אוֹ עָבֶה אוֹ צָרוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with a general rule about sounds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any natural sound of a שופר, whether high, deep, or rough, is acceptable.

steps.title: A ruling sent to the father of שמואל: a drilled horn works
steps.stepSummary: A ruling sent to the father of שמואל says that if someone drilled out a horn and blew it, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent a ruling to the father of שמואל: if he drilled it out and blew it, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about a שופר that was drilled out. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling sounds simple: a horn that was hollowed out by drilling can be used. The next step asks what this ruling is coming to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent to him (a ruling sent by letter)

phrases.english: They sent to the father of Shmuel:
If he drilled it out and blew it, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a drilled horn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A horn that was drilled out and then blown is acceptable for the מצוה.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious? Every שופר is drilled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling: it is obvious, since every שופר is drilled out anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! All of them are drilled too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling it just quoted. Why would anyone need to say this, if every שופר is made by drilling?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A horn taken from an animal has bone inside it, and that bone has to be removed before the horn can be blown. So drilling is part of making every שופר. This makes the ruling seem to teach nothing new.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
All of them, too, are drilled out, aren't they?
phrases.notes: The bone inside the horn has to be taken out, so every שופר gets drilled.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, כּוּלְּהוּ נָמֵי מִיקְדָּח קָדְחוּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in Step 24 for seeming to teach nothing new.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling sent to the father of שמואל that a drilled horn is acceptable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every שופר is drilled as part of how it is made, so saying a drilled horn is acceptable seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The case is where the bone core was drilled through
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the challenge: the ruling is about a horn whose inner bone core (זכרות) was drilled through rather than removed. Bone and horn are the same kind of material, so the bone does not count as a barrier.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: this is where he drilled through the bony core of the horn. You might have said that something of the same kind still counts as a barrier, so the ruling teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from the last step: why would anyone need to be told that a drilled-out horn is kosher?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal שופר has its bone core pulled out. Here the bone was left inside and a hole was drilled through it, so the sound passes through bone. We might have thought the bone blocks the horn, but the ruling teaches that the same kind of material does not count as a barrier (מין במינו אינו חוצץ).

keyTerms.meaning: the bony core that grows inside an animal's horn
a thing together with its own kind of material

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: where he drilled it through its bony core.
You might have said: a thing with its own kind is a barrier,
so it teaches us (that it is not).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25 by explaining the exact case of the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bone left inside the horn might count as a barrier, so the sound would come from bone and not from שופר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bone and horn are the same kind of material, so the bone is not a barrier and the person who blows has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.title: רב הונא limits the משנה about blowing into a pit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that blowing into a pit or cistern does not count. רב הונא says this applies only to people standing at the edge of the pit. Those standing inside the pit have fulfilled their obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who blows into a pit or cistern, and so on. רב הונא said: they taught this only about people standing at the edge of the pit. But people standing inside the pit have fulfilled their obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה: blowing a שופר into a pit. רב הונא explains whom that rule is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People outside the pit hear only an echo bouncing back, and an echo is not the sound of the שופר. People inside the pit hear the real שופר sound directly, so it counts for them. This means the משנה's 'not fulfilled' does not apply to everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is not arguing with the משנה. He is narrowing it: the משנה's 'not fulfilled' is only for people standing outside the pit.

phrases.aramaic: הַתּוֹקֵעַ לְתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַדּוּת כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: One who blows into a pit or into a cistern, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: they taught this only
about those standing at the edge of the pit,
but those standing in the pit have fulfilled their obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְאוֹתָן הָעוֹמְדִים עַל שְׂפַת הַבּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, about blowing into a pit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blowing into a pit fails only for listeners at the edge of the pit. Listeners inside the pit have fulfilled their obligation.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says blowing into a pit does count. It points out that this seems to clash with the משנה, which says it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: one who blows into a pit or cistern has fulfilled his obligation. But we learned in the משנה that he has not fulfilled it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a proof for רב הונא by putting the ברייתא next to the משנה. The two seem to say opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'fulfilled' and the משנה says 'not fulfilled' about the same case. Both cannot be true unless they describe different listeners. That is exactly רב הונא's distinction, and the next step draws the conclusion.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:

phrases.aramaic: הַתּוֹקֵעַ לְתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַדּוּת — יָצָא.
phrases.english: One who blows into a pit or into a cistern has fulfilled his obligation.
But we learned in the משנה: he has not fulfilled it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב הונא's ruling in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's distinction between people at the edge of the pit and people inside it
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says 'fulfilled', which clashes with the משנה's 'not fulfilled'

steps.title: The proof stands: it is like רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The only way to make the ברייתא and the משנה agree is רב הונא's distinction, so the גמרא concludes that his view is proven.
steps.simpleTranslation: So must we not learn from this that it is like רב הונא? Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof and confirms that רב הונא's explanation is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא must be talking about people inside the pit, and the משנה about people at the edge. Since this fits both sources, the גמרא accepts רב הונא's ruling as proven.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version of this passage, רב הונא's rule is proven from a ברייתא. People inside the pit hear the real שופר and have fulfilled their obligation. People at the edge hear only an echo and have not.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כִּדְרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this that it is like Rav Huna?
Yes, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כִּדְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof set up in step 28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא's distinction is proven: the משנה is about listeners at the edge of the pit and the ברייתא is about listeners inside it.

steps.title: Another version: the משנה and ברייתא contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: Some tell the passage differently. They do not present the ברייתא as support for רב הונא. Instead, they set it against the משנה as a contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some raise these sources as a contradiction. We learned in the משנה: one who blows into a pit or cistern has not fulfilled his obligation. But a ברייתא teaches: he has fulfilled it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same passage. In this version, it starts with a question about how the two sources can disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same two sources are used, but now nobody has made a distinction yet. The two sources simply clash, and the clash needs an answer, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: some raise them as a contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same material told a second way, as a contradiction instead of a proof.

phrases.english: Some raise them against each other as a contradiction.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: הַתּוֹקֵעַ לְתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַדּוּת — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: We learned: one who blows into a pit or into a cistern has not fulfilled his obligation.
But it was taught: he has fulfilled it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the passage of steps 27-29 in a different form, as a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that blowing into a pit does not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the same case does count, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: רב הונא resolves the contradiction
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that there is no contradiction. The משנה is about people at the edge of the pit, and the ברייתא is about people inside the pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: it is not difficult. Here, it is about those standing at the edge of the pit. There, it is about those standing inside the pit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the contradiction by saying each source is about a different group of listeners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב הונא's distinction is an answer to a contradiction rather than a ruling that was later proven. Either way the result is the same. Listeners at the edge hear only an echo and have not fulfilled their obligation, while listeners inside hear the real sound and have.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (there is no contradiction)
here... there (each source is about a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions reach the same law. For listeners standing inside the pit, blowing into a pit counts. For listeners standing at the edge, it does not.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: it is not difficult;

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — לְאוֹתָן הָעוֹמְדִין עַל שְׂפַת הַבּוֹר,
phrases.english: here, it is about those standing at the edge of the pit,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the משנה, which said 'not fulfilled'.

phrases.english: there, it is about those standing in the pit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source is about a different case (כאן... כאן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא disagree about blowing into a pit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about listeners at the edge of the pit and the ברייתא is about listeners inside it, so they do not disagree.

steps.title: רבה is introduced as the next speaker
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement in the name of רבה. His words follow right after this line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move: it tells us that רבה is about to say something on this topic. His actual statement comes in the next line of text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question of blowing into a pit was just settled through רב הונא's distinction between people at the edge and people inside the pit. Now a new אמורא, רבה, enters the discussion with his own comment. This line on its own does not yet contain any ruling. It only tells us who is speaking next.

keyTerms.meaning: A statement or teaching said by an אמורא.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רַבָּה (רבה) with רָבָא (רבא). They are two different אמוראים, and their names look almost the same.

phrases.english: Rabba said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב הונא settled the clash between the משנה and the ברייתא, the גמרא brings in a new speaker, רבה. His statement continues on the next עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling is stated yet. This line only introduces רבה as the speaker of the statement that follows.
